site.name: forge-coder
site.summary: Forge Coder — agentic coding IDE (local demo) Fictional agentic coding product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Agent run view Three-pane IDE-style layout: file tree (left) + agent chat (center) + live diff preview (right). Left — file tree: - Virtual TypeScript project (`atlas-cli`) with folder collapse, file-status badges (M for modified, + for newly added), and a summary footer. - Clicking any file marked M / + loads its diff into the right pane.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full forge-coder system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Forge Coder agent interface suffers from severe mobile usability issues, primarily a non-responsive three-pane layout that causes horizontal overflow and renders the interface nearly unusable on small screens. Critical agent controls lack proper state management and feedback; the 'Interrupt' button does not transform into a 'Resume' action when paused, and the 'Rerun' button provides zero visual feedback when clicked. Additionally, navigation tabs are non-functional dead links without active state indicators, leaving users disoriented and unable to trust the UI.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Forge Coder agentic IDE interface, validating the primary agent chat flow, file tree interactions, diff preview states, and responsive layout behavior.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first validating the primary agent run view and its interactive states (interrupt, rerun, chat). Next, it will deep-dive into the file tree and diff preview pane interactions, including view toggles and file selection. It will then test the top-level navigation tabs and header actions. Finally, the entire critical flow will be validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive layout and tap target issues identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The application is a single-page local demo where navigation tabs (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) may dynamically swap content or are placeholder controls.
Clicking files marked with 'M' or '+' in the file tree will update the right diff pane, while unmarked files may not.
The 'Interrupt' and 'Rerun' buttons will alter the agent's state visually in the UI, even if no real backend exists.
The 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox and chat input are functional UI controls that change the application's visual state.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets on mobile for file tree icons (⌕, +) and the 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox (13x13px)
Top navigation tabs (Agent, Inbox, Runs, Settings) which are small (50-70x32px) and may cause layout or interaction issues on mobile
State transition when 'Interrupt' or 'Rerun' is clicked—potential for broken or stalled UI states
Three-pane layout collapse behavior on mobile viewports

phases.title: Agent Run State & Chat Controls
phases.objective: Validate the primary agent run view, state transitions, and chat input functionality.
key_checks: Click '⏸ Interrupt' and verify the agent status updates appropriately
Click '↻ Rerun' and verify the run resets or restarts visually
Type a message in the 'Reply...' textarea and click 'Send'
Toggle the 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox on and off
exit_criteria: Agent state controls have been exercised
Chat input and submission work without errors

phases.title: File Tree & Diff Preview Interactions
phases.objective: Validate file tree navigation, folder collapse, file status badges, and the resulting diff preview updates.
key_checks: Click a folder (e.g., 'src' or 'upload') to collapse and expand it
Click a file marked 'M' (e.g., 'stream.ts') and verify the diff loads in the right pane
Click a file marked '+' (e.g., 'index.ts') and verify the diff loads
Click an unmarked file (e.g., 'retry.ts') and observe the right pane behavior
Click 'Accept all changes' and 'Open editor' buttons
exit_criteria: File tree interactions correctly update the diff pane
Diff view toggles function as expected
Diff action buttons have been clicked and observed

phases.title: Top Navigation & Header Actions
phases.objective: Validate the behavior of top-level tabs and header buttons.
key_checks: Click 'Inbox', 'Runs', and 'Settings' tabs to check for view changes or UI feedback
Click 'Agent' tab to return to the main view
exit_criteria: All top navigation tabs have been clicked
Header action buttons have been exercised

phases.title: Mobile Responsive Validation
phases.objective: Validate the layout, readability, and tap-target usability on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify the three-pane layout adapts correctly (e.g., panes stack or collapse)
Check if file tree and diff pane are accessible on mobile
Attempt to tap small controls identified in prescan (Auto-apply checkbox, nav tabs, tree icons)
Test chat input and send functionality on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been assessed for major usability flaws
Small tap target warnings have been visually confirmed
Core agent flow is functional on mobile

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 11 buttons, 4 links, 2 inputs, and key file tree interactions
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical agent, file tree, and diff checks on mobile viewport to validate layout and tap targets

notes: Prescan flagged 12 small tap target warnings, predominantly affecting the header nav, file tree icons, and the auto-apply checkbox; pay special attention to these during the mobile phase.
Since this is a local demo, 'Connect a repo' and 'Open in VS Code' may trigger external protocol handlers or simply fail gracefully; observe the UI reaction.

findings.user_goal: Use the IDE on a mobile device
findings.problem: The three-pane IDE layout does not adapt to mobile viewports, causing a horizontal overflow where the page width (733px) nearly doubles the mobile viewport (390px).
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag 'Page width 733px exceeds viewport 390px' during mobile testing (steps-37-42, steps-43-48, final observation). Crucial elements like 'Connect a repo' and 'Open in VS Code' have bounding boxes extending to x=636+, pushing them off-screen.
findings.why_it_matters: Users must scroll horizontally to access basic features, making the interface disorienting and practically unusable on mobile devices.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive layout that stacks the file tree, chat, and diff panes vertically on small screens, or hides the file tree/diff pane behind collapsible drawers.

findings.user_goal: Rerun a paused or finished agent task
findings.problem: Clicking the '↻ Rerun' button produces no visible state change, loading indicator, or status update, leaving the user wondering if the action was registered.
findings.evidence: In steps-01-06 and step agentic-47-click, clicking '↻ Rerun' resulted in 'No obvious URL or visible-text change' and the status remained 'Run #243 · paused'.
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of feedback for a critical action like rerunning an agent creates a trust gap. Users may click multiple times, leading to unintended duplicate runs or frustration.
findings.suggestion: Provide immediate visual feedback when 'Rerun' is clicked, such as a spinner on the button, a status change to 'Run #244 · running', or a toast notification confirming the rerun initiation.

findings.user_goal: Pause and resume an agent run
findings.problem: After pausing the agent, the '⏸ Interrupt' button remains labeled 'Interrupt' instead of changing to a 'Resume' or 'Continue' action.
findings.evidence: Session memory and step agentic-46-click show that clicking '⏸ Interrupt' transitions the status to 'paused', but the button text remains '⏸ Interrupt'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect a toggle control to reflect the reverse action. Showing 'Interrupt' when the agent is already paused is confusing and fails to afford the ability to resume the task.
findings.suggestion: Change the button label and icon to '▶ Resume' when the agent enters a paused state, clearly indicating the available next step.

findings.user_goal: Navigate between different views (Inbox, Runs, Settings)
findings.problem: Navigation tabs (Inbox, Runs, Settings) are dead links that append '#' to the URL without changing the view or providing any active state styling.
findings.evidence: In steps-07-12, clicking 'Inbox', 'Runs', and 'Settings' produced no visible UI change. The tabs also lack active state styling, making it impossible to know which view is selected.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead navigation links break user trust and create confusion. Users expect these tabs to provide access to run histories, settings, and messages, but instead, they lead to a dead end.
findings.suggestion: Either implement the underlying views for these tabs or remove/disable them with a clear visual indication (e.g., greyed out, 'Coming soon' tooltip) if they are not yet available.

findings.user_goal: Switch between Split and Unified diff views
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Split' or 'Unified' diff view toggles produces no visible change in the diff preview pane and lacks an active/selected state indicator.
findings.evidence: In steps-13-18, clicking 'Split' and 'Unified' produced no visible text or URL change, and there is no highlight or underline to distinguish the active toggle.
findings.why_it_matters: Without visual feedback or an active state, users cannot tell which diff mode they are currently viewing or if their click had any effect.
findings.suggestion: Add an active/selected visual state (e.g., background highlight or bold text) to the currently selected toggle, and ensure the diff pane visually updates when the mode is switched.

findings.user_goal: Interact with form controls on mobile
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements have tap targets well below the 44px mobile accessibility guideline, making them difficult to activate on touch devices.
findings.evidence: Final observation flags 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox (13x13px), file tree icons '⌕' (26x27px) and '+' (27x27px), nav links (32px height), and 'Send' button (59x34px) as failing mobile tap target guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Undersized tap targets lead to missed taps, accidental activations of adjacent controls, and a frustrating mobile experience, particularly for users with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding around interactive elements to meet the 44x44px minimum touch target size. For checkboxes like 'Auto-apply edits', wrap the label to expand the clickable area.

findings.user_goal: Type a multi-line reply to the agent
findings.problem: The chat textarea has a fixed, small height (38px), which constrains visibility for longer messages without auto-resizing behavior.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes the textarea (ux-11) has a relatively small height (38px) which might constrain visibility for longer user messages without auto-resizing behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot easily review or edit longer messages they are composing, leading to a cramped input experience and potential errors in their prompts.
findings.suggestion: Implement an auto-resizing textarea that grows vertically as the user types, up to a reasonable maximum height, before becoming scrollable.

gaps: 71% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
